extracted.intended_audience: general readers and historians interested in the North-West Mounted Police, Yukon gold rush, and late-19th-century Canadian frontier history
extracted.subtask_description: A chapter-length historical narrative describing actions, standards, and incidents involving the North-West Mounted Police during the Yukon gold rush and related frontier duties. Emphasis on operational practices, conduct, and institutional values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation of boat passage at Canyon and White Horse Rapids
rubrics_metrics.description: "No women or children will be taken in the boats. ... No boat will be permitted to go through the Canyon until the corporal is satisfied that it has sufficient free board to enable it to ride the waves in safety. No boat will be allowed to pass with human beings in it unless it is steered by competent men, and of that the corporal will be the judge. There will be a number of pilots selected ... and when a crew needs a man to steer them through the Canyon to the foot of the rapids, pilots will be taken in turn from that list. In the event of the men not being able to pay, the Corporal will be permitted to arrange that the boats are run without charge."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational safety rules set and enforced by police: restrict vulnerable passengers, require minimum vessel seaworthiness (freeboard), require competent steerage judged by the corporal, maintain an official pilot roster with rotation, and allow charitable waivers where pay cannot be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assertion of sovereignty and collection of customs on passes
rubrics_metrics.description: "He put Belcher on the Chilcoot and Strickland on the White Pass to hoist the British flag and collect customs levies ... all who wished to pass that way must contribute to the Dominion exchequer."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of police detachments to assert national jurisdiction at strategic points and to collect customs/revenue from travellers as a practical means of establishing and enforcing sovereignty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict enforcement with no tolerance for lawlessness
rubrics_metrics.description: Crimes, robberies and disorderly practices "suddenly ceased" at the Mounted Police line "because things of that sort would not be tolerated for a moment."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A compact, disciplined force operating without local entanglements enforces order firmly and immediately, deterring behaviour tolerated elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance and rescue of distressed travellers
rubrics_metrics.description: "We overtook some on the trail ... Many of them were staggering blindly along, with heavy loads on their backs ... These we assisted or they would have fallen by the way."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Police duty includes humanitarian assistance on trails (helping exhausted or lost migrants), preventing loss of life by direct aid during extreme conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of medical care and establishment of local hospital services
rubrics_metrics.description: "Dr. Grant ... treats hundreds of sick without remuneration. ... When he got into Dawson started the Good Samaritan Hospital with his own funds and became a large factor for the physical and moral well-being of the place."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medical relief (often unpaid) and local institutional health care are expected or supported to preserve force health and community welfare in remote posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure transport of gold and government funds (gold escorts)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The practice was to turn the gold into ingots and send these to the coast under care of the Mounted Police in small detachments of from two to six men. ... Not a mite ever went missing."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocols: standardize bullion form (ingots), use small trusted detachments, rigorous custody procedures and personnel selected for incorruptibility to ensure government funds' security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive patrolling to prevent loss and guide inexperienced migrants
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner Herchmer sent patrols over the Peace, Athabasca and Mackenzie rivers "in order to prevent the loss of any of these more or less inexperienced gold-seekers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preventive deployments and reconnaissance aimed at steering migrants to safer routes, discouraging hazardous attempts, and averting disasters before they occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endurance, judgment, and reliability expected of long patrols
rubrics_metrics.description: Moodie's patrol: long mixed-mode travel (horses, dogs, boats), extended hardship including running out of supplies and failing to find guides, ultimately taking a year and two months; the patrol "demonstrated again the endurance, judgment and reliability of the police."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patrol personnel must possess logistical adaptability, survival skill, perseverance, and sound judgment under protracted hardship and supply scarcity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication of laws, mail, and services to remote points
rubrics_metrics.description: Routledge's and other patrols were valuable in "taking in their mail and bringing it out and also in making known at remote points the laws that were specially applicable to their situation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patrols act as administrative links: disseminate legal obligations, deliver communications, and render services to isolated populations to maintain order and governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of presence, tact, and resource to influence behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: "The effect of even a single mounted policeman's personality upon a lawless mob requires to be seen to be fully appreciated, and there were countless occasions where the qualities of tact and readiness of resource were required to supplement the prestige which is begotten of discipline alone."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policing effectiveness combines authoritative presence with personal tact and improvisational problem-solving rather than relying on force alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair mediation of labour grievances and liaison with civil authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: "We tried our utmost to have the real grievances of the men settled, and my representations to the general manager of construction always met with prompt attention."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Police should act impartially to identify and forward legitimate grievances, facilitating prompt civil or managerial responses to reduce unrest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiative and inventive capacity in pursuit and law enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Constable Clisby, unable to use the ferry, "commandeered a railway hand-car" and improvised transport to continue pursuit and recapture an escaped prisoner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officers are expected to display resourcefulness and practical improvisation when standard means are unavailable to fulfil enforcement responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humility and understatement in official reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Official reports are "full of self-suppression" — e.g., Superintendent Wood's terse account of transporting $150,000 in gold: "I reached Victoria in due course and handed over the money."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A culture of modest, matter-of-fact reporting where dangerous or heroic actions are downplayed in official records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance domestic policing needs with overseas service obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: "For reasons known to the Dominion Government there was always necessity for keeping the larger part of the corps in Canada. They could not be allowed to enlist in a body for any war ... We put it in that way because ... we could not on either occasion let the whole Force go abroad."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deployment policy prioritizes maintaining homeland security and civil order; selective overseas service may be permitted but only after ensuring sufficient domestic coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for irregular warfare, scouting and patrol operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Mounted Police and ex-members "did conspicuous and distinctive service" on the veld, praised for scouting and patrol work; their frontier training gave "peculiar influence and prominence."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training and experience in frontier policing produces skills (scouting, irregular patrol, reconnaissance) directly transferable to certain military roles and irregular operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valor and gallantry under fire as demonstrated conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: Sergeant A. H. L. Richardson won the Victoria Cross by riding back under cross-fire to bring in a wounded comrade despite his own horse being badly wounded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extraordinary personal courage and self-sacrifice in rescue or combat situations are highlighted as the highest expressions of service and duty.
